According to Counterpoint Research data, although global smartphone shipments declined overall, Apple still accounted for nearly half of global smartphone revenue in the last quarter (Q2). Details are as follows.

Apple achieved its highest-ever revenue share record in Q2

Counterpoint Research published a new report (cited by MacMagazine) indicating that Apple's share of global smartphone revenue last quarter reached a historic high of 49%, representing a year-on-year revenue growth of 22%. This is the company's highest revenue share ever recorded in a second quarter.

Counterpoint noted that global smartphone revenue grew 7% year-on-year in that quarter, with Apple being the fastest-growing among the top five brands. Its average selling price rose from $879 a year ago to $946.

Apple's shipment share in Q2 also reached a historic high, rising from 17% to 21% compared to a year ago. However, Apple remained in second place, behind Samsung, which accounted for 23% of global shipments. The shipment shares of the other top five brands all declined, with Xiaomi seeing the largest drop, falling from 14% to 11%, with shipments decreasing 26% year-on-year.

Counterpoint pointed out that the entire industry is facing a memory shortage, with multiple smartphone manufacturers forced to raise prices due to rising component costs and tight supply. Apple iPhone pricing has remained largely stable, but Counterpoint expects this situation to change in the coming quarters.
